title: URL Shortener
summary: Alias-keyed link lifecycle and click accounting with durable command outcomes.
requirements: Create an alias for a target URL
Resolve and disable links
Record clicks and expose command outcomes
constraints: Bounded challenge contract; not a complete public URL platform
Alias is the state/depot routing key
invariants: One link record per alias
Replay of a request does not apply the command twice
acceptance: Create, resolve, disable, and click operations follow protocol results
Unknown aliases return the specified empty result
decisions: Store link state in $$links keyed by alias
tradeoffs: Alias colocation favors redirect and lifecycle state access; does not claim globally unique alias generation
seam: Redirect service consumes resolved target; HTTP handling is outside the module
queries: No query topology declared; wrapper uses direct foreign-select-one reads on $$links

read: client directly selects alias outcome/link/click count from $$links
flow.partition: Depot hash-by :alias; $$links outer key is alias. Same alias routes together; no additional topology partition claim.

caveat: Contract behavior comes from README/protocol; names and partitioning here are reference choices, not a claim about production-scale URL services.

title: Distributed Rate Limiter
summary: Per-user quota decisions consume capacity idempotently and expose limiter state.
requirements: Configure a user's limiter
Decide whether requests are allowed
Retain request decisions for replay safety
constraints: Contract is the bounded challenge protocol, not a production global quota system
invariants: A request id replay does not consume quota again
Quota decisions are associated with their user
acceptance: Decision and state queries match protocol semantics
decisions: Store limiter state in $$users keyed by user ID
tradeoffs: Per-user partitioning supports per-user atomic work, not a cross-user atomic quota
seam: Application enforces allow/deny result; no HTTP middleware is included
queries: No query topology; direct foreign-select-one reads of decisions and limiter state

read: client direct-selects decision or limiter from $$users
flow.partition: Depot hash-by :user-id; $$users outer key is user-id. This supports per-user colocation only.

caveat: Source-backed reference architecture; quota algorithm bounds are specified by README/protocol, not inferred from the handbook case study.

title: Notification System
summary: Tracks user preferences/devices, durable submissions, delivery effects, retries, and recent/dead-letter state.
requirements: Manage device generations and notification preferences
Submit notifications and process delivery effects
Track retries and dead letters
nonfunctional: Durable submissions and user delivery history
constraints: Submission records keyed by submission id; user view updates route by user
invariants: Stale device generation cannot supersede a newer generation
Effect processing is deduplicated by reference state
acceptance: Profile, submission, and status queries conform to protocol
Retry/dead-letter behavior follows the challenge contract
decisions: $$users stores profiles, recent history and dead letters
tradeoffs: Separate submission and user views support work tracking and user-facing history, with a routing hop
seam: External push/email/SMS provider is an integration boundary; delivery transport is not implied
queries: No query topology declared; direct foreign-select/select reads of $$users and $$submissions

write: effect path hash-routes by user and updates $$users
flow.partition: Depot hashes by :owner. Reference ETL explicitly |hash-routes *user before writing $$users; $$submissions is keyed by submission id and $$task-pos by Long; no broader colocation claim.

caveat: The source module implements durable work/state transitions; an external provider's delivery guarantees and actual network sending are outside this bounded module.

title: Web Crawler
summary: Host-keyed crawl state coordinates URL claims, crawl records, and host politeness.
requirements: Maintain crawl frontier and URL state
Claim work while enforcing host politeness
Deduplicate URL/claim processing
nonfunctional: Bound crawl operations by requested host/URL data
invariants: URL/claim state is associated with normalized host
Claim lifecycle and politeness follow protocol
acceptance: Claim, crawl/update, and query results meet README contract
decisions: Client reads PStates directly; no query topology
tradeoffs: Host affinity makes politeness coordination local to host, potentially concentrating a very hot host
seam: HTTP fetching, robots retrieval, and page parsing are external to the state module
queries: No query topology; wrapper directly selects claims, URL records, host info, and frontier range from $$hosts

write: core updates host info, URL/claim state and frontier
read: client directly selects host-scoped state and frontier pages from $$hosts
flow.partition: Depot hashes on :host and $$hosts outer key is host; module lower-cases host for claim lookup. No other partition strategy asserted.

caveat: Reference state machine only; no claim of a general web-scale fetch network or web-content index.

title: Search Autocomplete
summary: Locale-scoped phrase/session trends feed policy-filtered prefix ranking and phrase lookups.
requirements: Ingest versioned locale snapshots and session-deduplicated searches
Rank suggestions by prefix
Filter blocked phrases
nonfunctional: Bound prefix query output to requested k
constraints: Work-placement keys are generated by placement(locale, phrase/prefix)
invariants: A blocked phrase is not suggested
Session deduplication is scoped to locale/session per contract
acceptance: suggest and phrase query topology responses satisfy protocol
Stale snapshot generations do not replace current state
environment: Microbatch core and query topologies suggest/phrase
decisions: suggest and phrase are query topologies
tradeoffs: Placed phrase/prefix work balances updates, requiring placement routing for ETL and queries
seam: Search serving consumes suggestion results; document retrieval/ranking beyond phrase popularity is out of scope
queries: suggest (query topology; placement then |hash, reads generation/prefixes/blocked state)
phrase (query topology; placement then |hash, reads generation/blocked/phrase state)
owner metadata wrapper uses direct foreign-select-one on $$owner

write: placement routes phrase/prefix writes to relevant PStates
read: caller invokes suggest or phrase query topology
query placement and hash routing select locale/phrase partition
direct owner metadata select is separate from query topology
flow.partition: Depot hashes by locale; reference update/query paths calculate placement(locale, phrase or prefix) and |hash to that placed key. Distinct PStates have differing outer-key schemas; do not infer they share a physical partition absent matching placement.

caveat: The stored rankings and snapshot lifecycle are reference design choices implementing the bounded protocol, not a claim about a commercial search engine.

title: File Sync Service
summary: Namespace-partitioned file version, block metadata, request outcomes, and change journal with a file-head query.
requirements: Apply namespace-scoped file commands
Track versions and content blocks
Read current head and incremental journal changes
nonfunctional: Incremental reads avoid fetching full namespace history
invariants: File head/version lineage follows accepted writes
Request replay does not duplicate mutation
Block metadata remains addressable by hash
acceptance: Version, block, outcome, and journal reads follow protocol
tradeoffs: Namespace affinity enables command consistency; a large namespace can become a hot partition
seam: Block bytes/content transfer and client filesystem are external; module stores metadata
queries: outcome, block, version, and journal wrapper operations use direct foreign-select/select on $$namespaces

read: file-head uses query topology and namespace hash
other getters directly foreign-select namespace state
flow.partition: Depot hash-by :ns-id; query topology explicitly |hashes namespace; PState outer key is namespace id. These are aligned by source.

caveat: Metadata only. Distributed block storage and device synchronization transport are excluded.

title: Ticketing System
summary: Event-scoped seat inventory, expiring holds, and durable purchase/confirmation outcomes.
requirements: Hold and confirm/cancel seats
Prevent double allocation
Enforce hold deadlines and expose outcomes
nonfunctional: Durable request outcomes and compensation journal
constraints: Seat and hold queries are event-keyed
invariants: A seat cannot be sold/held by competing active reservations
Expired or stale holds cannot be confirmed
Idempotency prevents duplicate effects
acceptance: Seat and hold queries reflect command processing
Compensation and event sequencing match README
decisions: core groups and orders commands in microbatches
seats and hold query topologies route by event
tradeoffs: Event partitioning supports atomic event inventory but an extremely popular event concentrates work
seam: Payment authorization and external ticket delivery are outside the bounded inventory contract
queries: outcome, clock, compensation reads use direct foreign-select on $$events

write: core processes ordered per-event batch and updates $$events
read: seats/hold requests invoke dedicated query topologies
flow.partition: Depot hash-by :event-id, both query paths explicitly |hash event id, and $$events is keyed by event id. Alignment is directly source-backed.

caveat: This is the challenge's inventory/hold contract, not a complete ticket marketplace; transport, payment and delivery are not asserted.

title: Payment System
summary: Tenant-scoped idempotent payment commands create balanced immutable postings and account/journal views.
requirements: Process tenant payment commands
Maintain balanced immutable ledger postings
Read balances, charges, outcomes, and journal
constraints: Tenant is the depot and PState partition root
invariants: Each journal transaction balances
Postings are immutable
A replay cannot apply a payment twice
acceptance: Balance, charge, currency, outcome, and journal results match protocol
decisions: Client reads PStates directly; no query topology
tradeoffs: Tenant colocation supports transactional tenant ledger operations, while large tenants can be hot
seam: External bank/card processor and settlement are not included unless explicitly part of README contract
queries: No query topology; direct foreign-select/select reads for outcome, currency, account/balance, charge, and journal

flow.partition: Depot hash-by :tenant-id; $$tenants outer key is tenant id, giving tenant-key colocation per source.

caveat: Ledger correctness is the bounded challenge contract; do not infer bank-network settlement, PCI controls, or production payment-provider semantics.

title: Stock Exchange
summary: Symbol-partitioned limit-order matching maintains price levels, FIFO queues, trades, orders, and idempotent outcomes.
requirements: Submit/cancel limit orders
Match crossing orders using deterministic price-time priority
Expose depth, trades, orders, and outcomes
invariants: Trades satisfy crossing prices
Resting queues preserve price-time order
Trade sequence is monotonic per symbol
Cancellation removes only open owned order quantity
acceptance: GTC/IOC behavior, matching, cancellation, depth and trade paging follow protocol
decisions: $$symbols stores orders, bid/ask levels, queues, trades and requests
core groups and sorts commands by ingress position within each symbol
tradeoffs: Symbol-local matching keeps state changes ordered and atomic; hot symbols serialize more work
seam: Exchange connectivity, risk/margin checks, clearing and external market data are outside scope
queries: No query topology; wrapper uses direct foreign-select-one for outcome/order/depth/trades

write: core orders commands by symbol ingress position
read: client direct-selects outcomes/orders and bounded sorted depth/trade ranges
flow.partition: Depot hash-by :symbol and $$symbols outer key String symbol. Per-symbol grouping/ordering is in reference ETL; no account-wide partition claim.

caveat: Matching is scoped to one symbol per operation. Exchange regulation and the wider trading platform are outside scope.

title: Hotel Reservation System
summary: Property-scoped per-night inventory supports atomic half-open multi-night reservations, rate-locked bookings, cancellation, and event paging.
requirements: Configure property, room type, night capacity/rate
Reserve all nights in [checkin, checkout) atomically without overbooking
Lock booking total, cancel once, and page journal
nonfunctional: Work bounded by stay length and event page limit, not unrelated history
invariants: available = capacity minus confirmed booking quantities
Capacity is immutable after init
Cancellation restores exact quantity once
Journal seq contiguous; booking's reservation seq is immutable
acceptance: Reserve/cancel and availability reflect atomic night inventory
Reads return booking, outcome, and ordered bounded events
decisions: $$properties stores room types, nights, bookings, events and requests
core groups and orders property commands
tradeoffs: Property-key partitioning permits property-local atomic operations but makes a very large property a concentration point
seam: Search/ranking, payment authorization, physical room assignment, channel managers, and notifications are excluded

write: core orders commands and atomically updates property night inventory/booking/event/outcome state
read: availability invokes query topology which hashes property id
flow.partition: Depot hashes by :property-id; availability query explicitly |hashes property id; $$properties outer key is property id. Atomic night range operations are property-local in this reference design.

caveat: Contract forbids overbooking and excludes payment/search despite the handbook's broader hotel-system context; these exclusions are deliberate.
